Web Page for Du Pasquier & Hsu — Antibody Evolution (WASM)

Ultra-fast in-browser analysis of antibody variable domains in Xenopus laevis and Xenopus tropicalis. Featuring 123 Class I Functional Heavy Chain V-genes, 20 Heavy D-segments (DH1–DH9), 20 J-segments (JH & JL), and synthesis boundaries (TVSS / TVSA) with instant TSV export.

Louis Du Pasquier & Ellen Hsu

Basel Institute for Immunology (Switzerland) & SUNY Downstate (USA)

Louis Du Pasquier and Ellen Hsu pioneered the cellular and molecular understanding of ectothermic vertebrate immunity. Their seminal investigations using the clawed frog (Xenopus laevis and Xenopus tropicalis) elucidated how the adaptive immune system evolved, demonstrating somatic hypermutation mechanisms, polyploid Ig gene rearrangement, and identifying non-mammalian light chain lineages (Rho and Sigma).

Key Milestones in Amphibian Immunogenetics

1975 – 1985 (Basel Institute for Immunology)

Du Pasquier and colleagues establish Xenopus as the premier model for ontogeny and phylogeny of lymphocyte differentiation, demonstrating that tadpoles and adult frogs generate diverse antibody repertoires despite a limited number of lymphocytes.

1989 – 1994 (Ig Isotype Discovery & Repertoire Dynamics)

Discovery and cloning of IgX (the amphibian mucosal equivalent of IgA), IgY (the precursor to IgG and IgE), and the novel Rho (ρ) and Sigma (σ) light chain isotypes by Ellen Hsu, Louis Du Pasquier, and Joseph Schwager.

2000s – Present (Genomics & Somatic Hypermutation)

Complete mapping of the Xenopus tropicalis and Xenopus laevis immunoglobulin heavy (VH1–VH11, DH1–DH9, JH1–JH9 across Chr8.L and Chr8.S) and light chain loci, demonstrating the conservation of recombination signal sequences (RSS) and evolutionary divergence between ectothermic and endothermic antibody architectures.

Ectothermic vs. Endothermic Antibody Comparison

Feature Ectothermic (Xenopus) Endothermic (Mouse / Human)
Heavy Chain Isotypes IgM, IgX (mucosal), IgY (high affinity 7S), IgD IgM, IgD, IgG (1-4), IgA (1-2), IgE
Heavy Chain V Families VH1 through VH11 (>80 genes in genome) VH1 through VH7 (human) / VH1 through VH16 (mouse)
Heavy Chain D Elements DH1 through DH9 (Flanked by 12/12 bp spacer RSS) DH1 through DH7 (Flanked by 12/12 bp spacer RSS)
Heavy Chain J Elements JH1 through JH9 (Flanked by 23 bp spacer RSS) JH1 through JH6 (Flanked by 23 bp spacer RSS)
Light Chain Lineages Rho (ρ), Sigma (σ), Kappa (κ), Lambda (λ) Kappa (κ), Lambda (λ)
Somatic Hypermutation Moderate rate, selection in spleen (no germinal centers) High rate with follicular dendritic cell affinity maturation
